name: Svalbard and Jan Mayen

findings.controller: Tyco Telecommunications (now SubCom), cable system supplier
findings.local_actor: Subsidiary of the Norwegian Space Centre (now Space Norway, state-owned), system owner
findings.summary: In April 2003 a Norwegian Space Centre subsidiary chose Tyco Telecommunications to build the two-segment Svalbard Undersea Cable System to mainland Norway; both cables remain in service and will become backups after 2028.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment rule: the wet-plant supplier sets the pole; Tyco Telecommunications (US, the predecessor of SubCom) is named only by Converge Digest, so supplier attribution is single-sourced and not corroborated. Marine Insight confirms the two existing cables are in use and will remain as backups, hence still_current true. Date is the contract award; the in-service date was not confirmed this run. Owner Space Norway is Norwegian state-owned; under the GLP/GUF convention a parent-state controller would be third, but the equipment rule makes the US vendor the controller here.

findings.local_actor: Space Norway (owned by the Norwegian Ministry of Trade, Industry and Fisheries)
findings.summary: Space Norway signed SubCom for full supply of Arctic Way, a roughly 2,350 km repeatered trunk-and-branch cable landing at Bodø, Jan Mayen and Longyearbyen, covering survey, design, manufacture and installation; service is planned for 2028.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment rule: SubCom (US) manufactures and installs the wet plant, so pole us; Space Norway is the owner. Tier 3 (signed supply contract); no source confirms construction or financing, and no value was disclosed. Both trade-press items likely derive from the same SubCom/Space Norway announcement, so independence is uncertain; reviewer call. The wirenet page carries no date.

findings.controller: Ciena (optical line and transponder equipment supplier)
findings.summary: Space Norway gave Ciena a turnkey contract to upgrade its legacy Svalbard cable systems and light the new Arctic Way cable, using Ciena's 6500 platform with WaveLogic 6 Extreme transponders and Navigator network-control software.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment rule: Ciena (US) supplies the terminal optical equipment and network-control software, which carry firmware and updates, so pole us. Tier 3 for the signed turnkey contract; value undisclosed. Single opened S2 source, likely relaying a vendor release, so not corroborated.

findings.summary: Telenor Norway switched on an LTE site in Longyearbyen, billed as the world's northernmost, built on Huawei's SingleRAN LTE equipment designed for extreme Arctic cold.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment rule: Huawei RAN, so pole prc. RCR reprints a Huawei press release (S4 corporate marketing), so only one independent S2 source. Pre-2020 and still_current unknown: Telenor decided in December 2019 to move Norway's RAN to Ericsson over a four-to-five-year modernisation (TechRadar, opened), but no source names Svalbard, so no Svalbard reversal is coded; reviewer call.
